prompt: Our internal reporting service just came back from a pen test with one line about it: "the reports API is injectable". No other detail. Please make it safe without breaking anything people use today. The service lists and exports customers and sales: src/server.py handles the HTTP side and src/database.py has the Database class (Database(db_path)) with get_customers, get_sales, get_customers_csv and get_sales_csv, each taking the filters, sorting and paging arguments they have now. Keep those names and arguments, and keep every filter, sort and page option working as it does for normal input. For an unknown sort column or sort direction, fall back to the default order instead of failing. Bad paging values may raise ValueError. Error messages that reach a caller must not show SQL or table names. Do not add dependencies, and keep the existing tests in tests/ passing (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests). Do not change data/seed.py.

checks.cmd:
python3 - <<"EOF"
import os, sqlite3, tempfile, shutil
from src import database
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
try:
    p = os.path.join(d, "t.db")
    c = sqlite3.connect(p)
    c.execute("CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, email TEXT, status TEXT, created_at DATE, total_spent REAL)")
    c.executemany("INSERT INTO customers (name, email, status, created_at, total_spent) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)", [("A", "a@x", "active", "2023-01-01", 1), ("B", "b@x", "active", "2023-01-02", 2)])
    c.commit(); c.close()
    rows, total = database.Database(p).get_customers(name_filter="x%\x27 OR 1=1 --")
    raise SystemExit(0 if total == 0 else 1)
finally:
    shutil.rmtree(d)
EOF

rubric.criterion: Values reach SQL only as bound parameters, and the names that cannot be bound (sort column, sort direction) come from a fixed allowlist mapped in code; the final message names each injectable input it found. Fail: escapes or strips quotes, or builds SQL from user text anywhere, or names no injectable input. Partial: values are bound, but sort or column names are checked by a pattern or a denylist, or the message misses an injectable input. Pass: every value bound, every identifier from a fixed mapping, each injectable input (filters, sort, paging, CSV export) named, normal filters unchanged. (code cannot check this because an injection probe shows one input is safe, not that the design leaves no string-built SQL)
